description: Architecture review of the full benchmark suite — document structure, consistency, and design issues
steps: Step 1: Map the repository structure: list all directories under repo/, repo/benchmarks/, repo/notebooks/, repo/scripts/ and document their roles
Step 2: Identify shared code and cross-notebook dependencies — check imports in all repo/benchmarks/*/task_*.py files for shared modules, data loaders, scoring utilities
Step 3: Verify consistency of benchmark interfaces: every task_*.py must use @kbench.task() decorator, return valid types (bool/float/int/tuple), and follow the same scoring pattern
Step 4: Check for redundancies — duplicate utility functions, overlapping data files, or benchmarks that test the same construct
Step 5: Write findings to repo/ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW.md with sections: Structure, Dependencies, Interface Consistency, Redundancies, Recommended Changes

description: Notebook content audit — syntax-check and consistency review of all 33 notebooks in repo/notebooks/
steps: Step 1: List all .ipynb files in repo/notebooks/ and categorize by track (metacog_, learning_, attention_, exec_func_, social_cog_, other)
Step 2: For each notebook, run jupyter nbconvert --to notebook to validate JSON structure and syntax
Step 3: For each notebook, verify: cell 0 has pip install kaggle-benchmarks, has @kbench.task() decorator, final cell has %choose, no direct openai/anthropic imports
Step 4: Check scoring consistency within each track — do all metacog benchmarks use BSS? do all learning benchmarks normalize the same way?
Step 5: Flag incomplete notebooks (stub cells, placeholder text, TODO comments) and list in a table
Step 6: Write findings to repo/NOTEBOOK_AUDIT.md with per-notebook pass/fail table and list of issues to fix

description: Convert submission_overview.ipynb narrative content to markdown and integrate into SUBMISSION_NARRATIVE.md
steps: Step 1: Read repo/notebooks/submission_overview.ipynb and extract all markdown cells and code cell outputs
Step 2: Format extracted content as clean markdown with proper headings, tables, and citations
Step 3: Compare with existing repo/SUBMISSION_NARRATIVE.md — identify overlapping sections and unique content in each
Step 4: Merge unique content from submission_overview.ipynb into SUBMISSION_NARRATIVE.md in the appropriate sections
Step 5: Delete repo/notebooks/submission_overview.ipynb after successful merge
Step 6: Search all files for references to submission_overview.ipynb and update them to point to SUBMISSION_NARRATIVE.md

description: Submission requirements checklist — cross-reference competition rules against current state and produce final TODO for Ian
steps: Step 1: Fetch competition overview page at https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/kaggle-measuring-agi/overview and extract all submission requirements
Step 2: Read repo/CB_SUBMISSION_GUIDE.md and repo/IAN_TODO_FINAL.md for current known requirements and status
Step 3: For each requirement, check whether it is already done (per KNOWLEDGE-metacognition.md and project files) — mark as DONE, TODO, or BLOCKED
Step 4: Categorize remaining TODOs as must-do (blocks submission), should-do (improves score), nice-to-have
Step 5: Write the final checklist to repo/IAN_TODO_FINAL_v2.md with clear action items, estimated time per item, and priority order

description: Fix any notebook issues found in the audit — apply corrections to notebooks that fail SDK compatibility checks
steps: Step 1: Read repo/NOTEBOOK_AUDIT.md (produced by the audit task) and collect all notebooks with failures
Step 2: For each failing notebook: fix missing pip install cell, missing @kbench.task decorator, missing %choose cell, or unauthorized imports
Step 3: Re-run jupyter nbconvert --to notebook on each fixed notebook to confirm valid JSON
Step 4: For notebooks with inconsistent scoring within a track, align to the canonical scoring method documented in KNOWLEDGE (e.g., BSS for metacog confidence benchmarks)
Step 5: Update repo/NOTEBOOK_AUDIT.md with fix status for each issue
